answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The quill multiplier is published, charged in mesa, and inlet lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4775 identities would post 2336 proofs and burn roughly 76 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
